correctness.rationale: The update rule is explicit: at most two incorrect disjointness guesses discover previously missing target elements, each creating at most one false candidate; at most two later false-positive intersections can remove those false candidates. A depth-five shattered tree contradicts this four-error learner. Root-branch cardinalities 0,1,3,6 exclude excessive depths for n=3..6. Independently replayed standard-library verifier validates all 30 leaf paths in complete depth-1/2/3/4 trees on n=4/5/6/7; embedding the n=7 tree extends the lower bound to every larger n. No finite experiment is used for the infinite upper bound.

value.rationale: The exact online learnability of the canonical disjointness relation on pairs has a nontrivial stability threshold: optimal deterministic realizable mistakes grow 0,1,2,3,4 then remain four irrespective of ground-set size. The proof supplies both a simple uniform learner and an exact adaptive adversarial tree, giving a sharp algorithm-vs-adversary characterization. At n=7 four-level adaptive shattering occurs despite exhaustive failure of four-point nonadaptive VC shattering, illustrating why the sequential invariant contains information not captured by the conventional graph-neighborhood VC calculation. This is an exact natural finite-structure learning invariant, not an arbitrary enumerated slice.
